e-3055.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
e-3055.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle \sin^3{t}, \:\cos^3{t} \right\rangle$ at an arbitrary point where $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
e-3055.worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)= x(t) \,\mathbf i + y(t) \,\mathbf j,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by 

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $\mathbf r(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{3}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{3}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3{cos}^{2}⁡t(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\ \text{ } & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{1} \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

 

In the last step, we were able to remove the absolute value bars because $\sin{t}>0$ and $\cos{t}>0$ for $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

e-3056.knowledge_point: Finding Unit Tangent Vectors Using the Rules of Differentiation For Vector Functions
e-3056.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=e^{2t}\mathbf p(t)$ at the point where $t=0,$ if $\mathbf p(0)=\mathbf i-\,\mathbf j-\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf p'(0)=\mathbf i - \mathbf j+ 2\mathbf k.$
e-3056.worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)=x(t)\mathbf i+y(t)\mathbf j+z(t)\mathbf k,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find $\mathbf r'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})p(t)+{e}^{2t}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}p(t)+{e}^{2t}{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =2{e}^{2(0)}p(0)+{e}^{2(0)}{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =2(i-\,j-k)+1(i-j+2k) \\  & =3\,i-3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot {3}^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}(3\,i-3\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is $\mathbf T(0) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\mathbf i -  \mathbf j).$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨2t,4sin⁡2t,4cos⁡2t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞)?

a
 117⟨1,4cos⁡2t,−4sin⁡2t⟩
b
 117⟨t2,2cos⁡2t,−2sin⁡2t⟩
c
 217⟨t,2cos⁡2t,−2sin⁡2t⟩
d
 117⟨1,4cos⁡2t,−4sin⁡2t⟩
e
 117⟨t,cos⁡2t,−sin⁡2t⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate: r'(t)=⟨2,8cos(2t),−8sin(2t)⟩. Its magnitude is √(4+64cos²(2t)+64sin²(2t))=2√17. Thus T(t)=r'(t)/‖r'(t)‖=(1/√17)⟨1,4cos(2t),−4sin(2t)⟩, which is option a.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨2t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+(8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+{(-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64{cos}^{2}⁡2t+64{sin}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+16({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+16} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{17}}⟨2,\,8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}⟨1,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨2t,4sin⁡2t,4cos⁡2t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞)?

a
 117⟨1,4cos⁡2t,−4sin⁡2t⟩
b
 117⟨t2,2cos⁡2t,−2sin⁡2t⟩
c
 217⟨t,2cos⁡2t,−2sin⁡2t⟩
d
 117⟨1,4cos⁡2t,−4sin⁡2t⟩
e
 117⟨t,cos⁡2t,−sin⁡2t⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(4sin⁡2t),ddt(4cos⁡2t)⟩=⟨2,8cos⁡2t,−8sin⁡2t⟩

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t): ‖r′(t)‖=(2)2+(8cos⁡2t)2+(−8sin⁡2t)2=4+64cos2⁡2t+64sin2⁡2t=21+16(cos2⁡2t+sin2⁡2t)=21+16=217

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve: T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=1217⟨2,8cos⁡2t,−8sin⁡2t⟩=117⟨1,4cos⁡2t,−4sin⁡2t⟩

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms r'(t)=⟨2,8cos(2t),−8sin(2t)⟩ and ‖r'(t)‖=2√17. Dividing gives option a, which has unit magnitude for every real t. The observed incorrect submission was option b.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨2t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+(8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+{(-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64{cos}^{2}⁡2t+64{sin}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+16({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+16} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{17}}⟨2,\,8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}⟨1,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=ti+t2j at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
11+4t2(i+2tj)
b
11+t2(i+tj)
c
11+2t2(i+tj)
d
11+4t2(i−2tj)
e
11+4t2(ti+t2j)
Submit

decision.explanation: The derivative is r'(t)=i+2t j, with magnitude √(1+4t²). Normalizing gives T(t)=(i+2t j)/√(1+4t²), so option a is valid for every real t.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j \\  & =i+2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}(\,i+2t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=ti+t2j at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
11+4t2(i+2tj)
b
11+t2(i+tj)
c
11+2t2(i+tj)
d
11+4t2(i−2tj)
e
11+4t2(ti+t2j)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=ddt(t)i+ddt(t2)j=i+2tj

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=12+(2t)2=1+4t2

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=11+4t2(i+2tj)

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j \\  & =i+2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}(\,i+2t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨tsin⁡t−cos⁡t,tcos⁡t+sin⁡t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
 12+t2⟨sin⁡t+cos⁡t,cos⁡t−sin⁡t⟩
b
 14+t2⟨2sin⁡t−tcos⁡t,−2cos⁡t⟩
c
 11+t2⟨cos⁡t,−tsin⁡t⟩
d
14+t2⟨2sin⁡t+tcos⁡t,2cos⁡t−tsin⁡t⟩
e
 11+t2⟨tcos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: By the product rule, r'(t)=⟨2sin(t)+tcos(t),2cos(t)−tsin(t)⟩. Its squared magnitude is 4sin²(t)+4cos²(t)+t²cos²(t)+t²sin²(t)=4+t², since the cross terms cancel. Normalizing gives option d for every real t.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t-2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨tsin⁡t−cos⁡t,tcos⁡t+sin⁡t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
14+t2⟨2sin⁡t+tcos⁡t,2cos⁡t−tsin⁡t⟩
b
 11+t2⟨tcos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩
c
 11+t2⟨cos⁡t,−tsin⁡t⟩
d
 14+t2⟨2sin⁡t−tcos⁡t,−2cos⁡t⟩
e
 12+t2⟨sin⁡t+cos⁡t,cos⁡t−sin⁡t⟩
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=⟨ddt(tsin⁡t−cos⁡t),ddt(tcos⁡t+sin⁡t)⟩=⟨sin⁡t+tcos⁡t+sin⁡t,cos⁡t−tsin⁡t+cos⁡t)⟩=⟨2sin⁡t+tcos⁡t,2cos⁡t−tsin⁡t⟩

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(2sin⁡t+tcos⁡t)2+(2cos⁡t−tsin⁡t)2=4sin2⁡t+2tsin⁡tcos⁡t+t2cos2⁡t+4cos2⁡t−2tcos⁡tsin⁡t+t2sin2⁡t=4(sin2⁡t+cos2⁡t)+t2(cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t)=4+t2

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=14+t2⟨2sin⁡t+tcos⁡t,2cos⁡t−tsin⁡t⟩

verification.explanation: Differentiation gives r'(t)=⟨2sin(t)+tcos(t),2cos(t)−tsin(t)⟩. The squared magnitude is 4+t²; the cross terms ±4t sin(t)cos(t) cancel. Normalizing confirms the revealed final answer. This expression is option d in the supplied JSON and option a in the reordered screenshot.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t-2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=ti+(2−t)j at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞).

a
 11+4t(i−j)
b
 11+4t(3i+2tj)
c
 11+4t(ti−2tj)
d
 11+4t(i−2tj)
e
 11+4t(i−tj)
Submit

decision.explanation: r'(t)=i/(2√t)−j. For t>0, its magnitude is √(1+4t)/(2√t). Dividing gives T(t)=(i−2√t j)/√(1+4t), which is option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\sqrt{t}\,i+(2-t)\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-t)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i-\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4t}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+4t}{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+4t}}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}i-\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(i-2\sqrt{t}\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=ddt(t)i+ddt(2−t)j=12ti−j

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(12t)2+(−1)2=14t+1=1+4t4t=1+4t2t

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=2t1+4t(12ti−j)=11+4t(i−2tj)

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\sqrt{t}\,i+(2-t)\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-t)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i-\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4t}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+4t}{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+4t}}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}i-\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(i-2\sqrt{t}\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=t2i+5tj at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
 14t2+25(ti+2j)
b
 1t2+5(2ti+5j)
c
 14t2+25(ti+5t2j)
d
 14t2+25(ti+5j)
e
 14t2+25(2ti+5j)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=ddt(t2)i+ddt(5t)j=2ti+5j

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(2t)2+(5)2=4t2+25

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=14t2+25(2ti+5j)

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+5t\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t)\,j \\  & =2t\,i+5\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+25}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+25}}(2t\,i+5\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨cos⁡t+tsin⁡t,sin⁡t−tcos⁡t,32t2⟩ at the point where t=π.

a
⟨312,0,312⟩
b
⟨−12,0,32⟩
c
⟨12,0,32⟩
d
⟨−312,0,312⟩
e
⟨−27,0,37⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives r'(t)=⟨tcos(t),tsin(t),√3 t⟩. At t=π, this is ⟨−π,0,√3 π⟩ with magnitude 2π. Normalizing gives ⟨−1/2,0,√3/2⟩, option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi .$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\sqrt{3}t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{(-\pi )^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨cos⁡t+tsin⁡t,sin⁡t−tcos⁡t,32t2⟩ at the point where t=π.

a
⟨312,0,312⟩
b
⟨−12,0,32⟩
c
⟨12,0,32⟩
d
⟨−312,0,312⟩
e
⟨−27,0,37⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖

First, we find r′(t) and evaluate it at t=π: r′(t)=⟨ddt(cos⁡t+tsin⁡t),ddt(sin⁡t−tcos⁡t),ddt(32t2)⟩=⟨−sin⁡t+sin⁡t+tcos⁡t,cos⁡t−cos⁡t+tsin⁡t,32⋅2t⟩=⟨tcos⁡t,tsin⁡t,3t⟩r′(π)=⟨πcos⁡π,πsin⁡π,3π⟩=⟨−π,0,3π⟩ Now, we calculate the magnitude of r′(π): ‖r′(π)‖=(−π)2+(0)2+(3π)2=4π2=2π

Finally, we normalize r′(π) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where t=π:

T(π)=r′(π)‖r′(π)‖=12π⟨−π,0,3π⟩=⟨−12,0,32⟩

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi .$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\sqrt{3}t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{(-\pi )^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

What is the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨t4,t2,4t⟩ at the point P(1,1,4)?

a
⟨23,13,0⟩
b
⟨13,23,23⟩
c
⟨26,16,16⟩
d
⟨23,13,23⟩
e
⟨23,23,13⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Since 4t=4, the point corresponds to t=1. The derivative is r'(t)=⟨4t³,2t,4⟩, so r'(1)=⟨4,2,4⟩ has magnitude √(16+4+16)=6. Normalizing gives ⟨2/3,1/3,2/3⟩, option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ at the point $P(1,1,4)?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

{t4=1t2=14t=4.

From the third equality, we get t=1. This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point P(1,1,4) is at the tip of r(1).

Now, we calculate r′(t) and evaluate it at t=1:

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
content.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ at the point $P(1,1,4)?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The first coordinate gives t=2π. Differentiating yields r'(t)=i−sin(t)j+cos(t)k, so r'(2π)=i+k has magnitude √2. Normalizing gives (√2/2)i+(√2/2)k, option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ at the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k \\ t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2\pi  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t=1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2\pi .$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ is at the tip of $r(2\pi ).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2\pi ) & =\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )\,k \\  & =i+0\,j+\,k \\  & =i+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+0+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2\pi ,1,0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot (i+k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ at the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k \\ t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2\pi  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t=1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2\pi .$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ is at the tip of $r(2\pi ).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2\pi ) & =\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )\,k \\  & =i+0\,j+\,k \\  & =i+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+0+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2\pi ,1,0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot (i+k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The point P(2,1,1) corresponds to t=1. Differentiating gives r'(t)=2i+2t j+k, so r'(1)=2i+2j+k has magnitude √(4+4+1)=3. Normalizing gives option d.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k$ at the point $P(2,1,1)?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,1,1)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+\,j+\,k \\ 2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k & =2\,i+\,j+\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ t=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,1,1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =2\,i+2t\,j+\,k \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =2\,i+2(1)\,j+\,k \\  & =2\,i+2\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,1,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2\,i+2\,j+\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{2}{3}\,j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
content.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k$ at the point $P(2,1,1)?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,1,1)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+\,j+\,k \\ 2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k & =2\,i+\,j+\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ t=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,1,1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =2\,i+2t\,j+\,k \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =2\,i+2(1)\,j+\,k \\  & =2\,i+2\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,1,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2\,i+2\,j+\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{2}{3}\,j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

a

decision.explanation: The point corresponds to t=2. Differentiating gives r'(t)=i+2t j+4t k, so r'(2)=i+4j+8k has magnitude √(1+16+64)=9. Normalizing gives option a.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k$ at the point $P(2,4,8)?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,4,8)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k \\ t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=4 \\ 2{t}^{2}=8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =i+2t\,j+4t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2) & =\,i+2\cdot 2\,j+4\cdot 2\,k \\  & =i+4\,j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{81} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,4,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2)}{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (i+4\,j+8\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\,i+\frac{4}{9}\,j+\frac{8}{9}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
content.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k$ at the point $P(2,4,8)?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,4,8)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k \\ t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=4 \\ 2{t}^{2}=8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =i+2t\,j+4t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2) & =\,i+2\cdot 2\,j+4\cdot 2\,k \\  & =i+4\,j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{81} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,4,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2)}{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (i+4\,j+8\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\,i+\frac{4}{9}\,j+\frac{8}{9}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 11
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=(t2−2t)p(t) at the point corresponding to t=1, given that p(1)=i+2j−k and p′(1)=2i−j−2k.

a
33(−2i+j+2k)
b
−2i+j+2k
c
−19i+19j+29k
d
33(2i−j−2k)
e
−23i+13j+23k
Submit

decision.explanation: By the product rule, r'(t)=(2t−2)p(t)+(t²−2t)p'(t). At t=1, r'(1)=−p'(1)=−2i+j+2k, whose magnitude is 3. Normalizing gives option e.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=1$, given that  $p(1)=i+2\,j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(1)=2\,i-\,j-2\,k.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =(2t-2)\,p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =(2(1)-2)\,p(1)+((1)^{2}-2(1))\,{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =0-{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =-(2\,i-\,j-2\,k) \\  & =-2i+\,j+2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-2\,i+j+2k) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is  $T(1)=-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k.$

EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖

First, we find r′(t) and evaluate it at t=1:

r′(t)=ddt((t2−2t)p(t))=ddt(t2−2t)⋅p(t)+(t2−2t)⋅ddt(p(t))=(2t−2)p(t)+(t2−2t)p′(t)r′(1)=(2(1)−2)p(1)+((1)2−2(1))p′(1)=0−p′(1)=−(2i−j−2k)=−2i+j+2k

Now, we calculate the magnitude of r′(1):

‖r(1)‖=(−2)2+(1)2+(2)2=9=3

Finally, we normalize r′(1):

T(1)=r′(1)‖r′(1)‖=13⋅(−2i+j+2k)=−23i+13j+23k

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to t=1 is T(1)=−23i+13j+23k.

content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=1$, given that  $p(1)=i+2\,j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(1)=2\,i-\,j-2\,k.$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =(2t-2)\,p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =(2(1)-2)\,p(1)+((1)^{2}-2(1))\,{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =0-{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =-(2\,i-\,j-2\,k) \\  & =-2i+\,j+2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-2\,i+j+2k) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is  $T(1)=-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k.$
